title: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: MVP scope + launch criteria
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Context
We need an automated safety rail that ties rollout operations (canary + A/B + staged model deployments) to latency/error-rate SLO monitors. As more customers run aggressive rollouts, manual mitigation is too slow and risks SLA violations. This MVP wires monitoring -> decision -> action with auditability and Console visibility.

Customer signal / impact
- Support: SUP-19422 (canary rollout latency regression; requested auto mitigation)
- Support: SUP-19458 (5xx spike during A/B; asked for configurable thresholds + visibility)
- Customer deep dive transcript: sources/fireflies/customer-success/2026-02-06-slo-driven-auto-rollback-technical-deep-dive.json
Primary impact: reduce customer-facing latency regressions during rollouts; reduce SRE/service-owner MTTR.

MVP goals (what we will ship)
1) Automatic action on SLO breach for eligible rollouts
- When a rollout step is active (canary or A/B), the rollout controller evaluates configured SLO monitors scoped to the rollout (route/service + model version + region + customer tier).
- On breach that meets evaluation rules (burn-rate windows + min sample + debounce), the system triggers ONE of:
  a) Pause rollout at current step (default for MVP)
  b) Rollback traffic to baseline / last-known-good (enabled behind flag for internal services first)
- Idempotent execution: repeated evaluations must not cause oscillation or double-execute rollback.

2) Policy configuration (MVP UX + semantics)
- Add an "Auto actions" section to rollout policy config with:
  - Enable/disable auto actions
  - Choose action type: pause or rollback (rollback gated)
  - Select SLO signals: p95 latency, p99 latency, error rate (5xx) (saturation optional, if already supported by SLO tooling)
  - Evaluation defaults: fast burn + slow burn windows; minimum request count; holdoff/debounce
  - Suppression: manual admin-only suppression window with required justification
- Provide safe defaults + guardrails (bounds) to prevent accidental flapping.

3) Audit trail + Console visibility
- Every evaluation cycle produces an auditable record when it results in a decision or when a decision is suppressed.
- Console surfaces:
  - Rollout timeline shows: "Auto-paused due to SLO breach" / "Auto-rollback executed" / "Auto action suppressed"
  - Event detail includes: which monitors/signals, evaluation window summary, policy version, timestamp, and links to dashboards.

4) Operational readiness
- Dashboards + alerts for:
  - auto action triggered
  - action suppressed
  - monitor missing/stale
- Runbook for oncall triage + how to override/suppress + safe reattempt.
- Game day in staging validating: latency spike, error spike, monitor staleness, telemetry lag.

Explicit non-goals (MVP)
- Quality/evals-driven rollback (handled in separate guardrails workstream)
- Fully autonomous multi-region failover (beyond pause/rollback in-scope rollout)
- Complex multi-signal scoring/ML-based anomaly detection; we use explicit SLO burn-rate logic
- Customer self-serve advanced templates library (we will ship 1–2 recommended presets only)

Product requirements (functional)
A) Eligibility and gating
- Feature flag gating by environment and service allowlist (internal routes first).
- Rollout must have valid monitor coverage for the rollout scope; if missing/stale, default behavior is "no auto action" + emit alert/rollout event (see decision notes below).

B) Evaluation semantics (MVP)
- SLO burn-rate evaluation with two windows (fast + slow) and minimum sample sizes.
- Debounce/holdoff to prevent flapping (e.g., require breach to persist for N eval cycles OR for a minimum duration).
- "Do not rollback during known incident" override: MVP approach is admin suppression with justification (incident integration later).

C) Actions
- Pause action: stop advancing rollout steps; keep traffic split stable; require manual operator to resume.
- Rollback action (gated): revert traffic to baseline/last-known-good using safe step-down strategy.

D) Audit and access control
- Auto actions must be visible to operators; suppression/override is admin-only.
- Audit events must not leak customer content; only IDs and metric references.

Success metrics (MVP)
- Internal: median time-to-mitigate rollback-class rollout regressions reduced to < 5 minutes (from first breach -> action recorded).
- Customer-facing: reduction in incidents where rollouts cause sustained p95/p99 regressions that breach SLO for > 10 minutes (tracked for opted-in routes).
- Guardrail: < 1% false-positive auto actions on internal canary routes during first 2 weeks after enabling.

Launch criteria / checklist
Must-have before enabling in production for any customer-serving route:
- [ ] Monitors exist and are tagged/scope-queryable for route/model/region/tier (coverage audited)
- [ ] Burn-rate endpoint supports rollout scoping (slo-toolkit)
- [ ] Decision audit events emitted and visible in Console timeline
- [ ] Alerts routed to correct Slack channels; no paging storms (notify vs page defined)
- [ ] Runbook published + oncall training completed
- [ ] Staging E2E tests: injected latency + error spikes trigger pause; rollback path validated for internal allowlist
- [ ] Backout plan: feature flag off + controller safe behavior verified

Phased rollout plan (MVP)
Phase 0 (dev/staging): pause-only; synthetic signals; validate audit log + UI.
Phase 1 (internal prod allowlist): pause default; rollback enabled for 1–2 internal routes with tight guardrails.
Phase 2 (selected customer tiers): dedicated/private opt-in only; require SRE sign-off per service.

Open questions
1) Missing/stale monitor behavior: fail-open (no auto action) vs fail-closed (pause). Current MVP proposal: fail-open + emit "monitor missing/stale" event + alert, to avoid freezing rollouts due to telemetry outages. Needs explicit SRE sign-off.
2) Default action by tier: self-serve hosted = pause; dedicated/private = pause (MVP) with optional rollback after validation.
3) Which latency percentile is primary: p99 is noisy for low volume; propose p95 primary + p99 optional with higher min-sample.

comments: 2026-02-07 (Marissa Cole): Created MVP ticket after escalation from SUP-19422. Key requirement: operators must see "why" we paused/rolled back with links to dashboards. Rolling back without auditability is a non-starter for enterprise.

2026-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): SRE view: default should be pause-only until we validate rollback executor idempotency under partial failures. Also strongly prefer min-sample gating; p99 is too spiky at low QPS. +1 to dual-window burn-rate.

2026-02-12 (Paula Mendes): Added explicit launch checklist and phased rollout. Aligning with Release Eng that monitor coverage gating should be part of enablement. Proposed fail-open on missing/stale monitor (emit event + alert) pending ADR sign-off.

2026-02-14 (Aisha Bello): For alerts: page only on "rollback executed" for internal allowlist; otherwise notify in #eng-sre and service channel. Need distinct alert for "monitor stale" because that was root cause in the 2/17 simulation.
2026-02-18 (Jada Williams): Controller hook will initially emit pause decisions only behind feature flag. Rollback path will be separate flag and requires ENG-4829 + ENG-4850 completion.

2026-02-21 (Connor O'Brien): Release gating proposal: do not allow enabling auto actions for a route unless dashboards + alerts are deployed and runbook link is provided in service config. Please capture in PM-618 templates + policy editor UX.
